correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=2 and 1<=k<m and real 0<t<1, box-section vertex classification gives exactly two orbits. Strict convexity and permutation symmetry reduce the minimum Euclidean covering ball to the max of exact orbit-distance quadratics. The affine difference determines a sharp threshold and all contact cases; independent exact-rational enumeration and minimax candidate checks replayed 308 test cases. Finite checks are corroborative, not substitutes for the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The natural full continuous one-coordinate cap family loses hypersimplex vertex transitivity and acquires fractional vertices. The theorem gives its unique exact Euclidean minimum ball, a nontrivial delayed phase transition from screened to all-vertex contacts, precise multiplicities and squared screening gap, and a C1-not-C2 radius profile; these are structural covering-geometry statements, not only a one-off numerical or textbook endpoint computation.
